newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony Computer boosting game player output.
newsitem.headline: Sony Computer boosting game player output.

text.p: Sony Computer Entertainment Inc said on Wednesday that it would boost output of its popular PlayStation game players in Japan after it stopped production in the United States.
The company, a unit of Sony Corp, said the move would enable it to achieve greater economies of scale by concentrating manufacturing of the 32-bit game console in Japan.
"We are increasing output in Japan, aiming to boost the scale of production," a spokesman said.
Increased demand for the player also means Sony Computer will boost output of the game player in Japan at a faster pace than originally planned, a spokesman said.
Sony initially planned to boost its PlayStation output to 700,000 units a month but will raise that figure, he said.
Sony Computer stopped making PlayStations abroad when it recently halted production at its San Diego plant.
Earlier this month, Sony Computer said that it would start selling its game machine and software in Asian markets outside of Japan from early December.
The PlayStations and game software titles will be sold initially in Hong Kong, Singapore, Thailand and Malaysia.
